lastMessage:
Fixed â€” with a real bug found and closed along the way

Before: speak-response.ps1 ran the full cycle (edge-tts synthesis â†’ probe duration â†’ Start-Sleep -Seconds $duration â†’ write "idle") inline, blocking the hook for the entire spoken length of the response. 131 of 133 recent runs hit the 60s timeout and got killed mid-sleep.

What I did:
1. Split the hook into speak-response.ps1 (fast dispatcher) and a new speak-response-worker.ps1 (does the slow work). The dispatcher reads the transcript, extracts/cleans the text, and hands off to the worker as a fully detached background process (Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden), then exits immediately â€” no more Start-Sleep on the hook's own execution path.
2. Added single-speaker queueing: before launching a new worker, the dispatcher kills any still-running previous one via taskkill /T /F (kills the whole process tree, not just the parent, so an edge-tts subprocess can't linger).

Bug I found while testing, not just assumed fixed: the first version killed the previous worker but both workers wrote to the same fixed latest.mp3 path. When a long-response worker got killed mid-synthesis by a following short response, the new worker could end up probing the old, much longer file for its duration â€” I reproduced this live: a worker for a ~30-word sentence ended up sleeping for 342 seconds because it read a stale file. Fixed by having each worker synthesize to its own uniquely-named temp file, probe that file's duration, and only then copy it into latest.mp3. I also closed a related temp-file leak (a killed worker can't run its own cleanup) by having the dispatcher delete the previous worker's temp files itself.

Verified live, not just by inspection:
- Short response: dispatcher returns in ~1.3s (was: blocks for full audio length).
- Long response (~200 words, audio >60s): dispatcher still returns in <1s; the detached worker was confirmed still running and correctly mid-sleep 126+ seconds later â€” proof it now survives past the old timeout ceiling.
- Adversarial retest (long worker killed mid-synthesis by a short one 2s later): worker A's process tree confirmed fully gone, worker B correctly slept ~3.8s (matching its own short text) instead of inheriting A's stale duration, and zero leftover temp files afterward.

Nothing else in your hook config was touched.
